M1: Introduction to Sustainable Energy System Transformation
Chapter 3 Overview

his chapter explores the core policy instruments and tools that drive sustainable energy transitions, structured across three categories: regulatory (command-and-control), market-based, and contractual/procurement mechanisms.
It examines how tools like Renewable Portfolio Standards, Carbon Taxes, Feed-in Tariffs, and Power Purchase Agreements can be designed to align with national contexts and development priorities.

Lesson 1: Planning and Strategic Instruments
This lesson introduces key national instruments used to plan and implement sustainable energy transitions, including long-term strategies, national energy policies, and sectoral action plans.

It examines how countries set energy and climate goals, align them with development priorities, and operationalize them through tools like renewable energy plans, efficiency strategies, and clean cooking roadmaps.

Lesson 2: Command-And- Control Instruments
Regulations form the backbone of the energy transition by setting clear rules that shape how energy is produced, distributed, and consumed.
This lesson explores command-and-control instruments which set enforceable targets to drive clean energy adoption.
While these tools ensure compliance, modern designs increasingly combine strict mandates with market flexibility to encourage innovation.

Through global examples like South Korea, Pakistan, and Barbados, we examine how well-designed regulations can deliver climate goals, economic benefits, and energy justice, especially in developing contexts where policy clarity and institutional capacity are vital.

Lesson 3: Market-Based Instruments
Market-Based Instruments (MBIs) use prices and incentives to drive clean energy and reduce emissions.
Unlike rigid regulations, they let actors choose cost-effective solutions.
This lesson covers key MBIs—Feed-in Tariffs, Emissions Trading Systems, and Carbon Taxes—and shows how they promote innovation, attract investment, and support flexible, efficient energy transitions.

Lesson 4: Key Contractual Tools

This lesson explores contractual and procurement instruments—such as Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), Independent Power Producers (IPPs), Public–Private Partnerships (PPPs), and Build–Own–Operate/Transfer (BOO/BOT) models, as key tools to mobilize private capital for sustainable energy.
These instruments structure public-private relationships, reduce risks, and enable long-term investments.
In developing countries, where public funds are limited, their effective use is essential to accelerate clean energy deployment and ensure a just energy transition.
